messages:
perf-bot: Nightly perf alert: serving-prod-n1 p99 latency up +35% vs baseline since 03:00 UTC. Throughput stable, tail spike. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prod/serving-n1 (alert id: A-6221)

maria: seeing the same in traces, looks like longer kernel runtime on long sequences. noticed kernel-selector flagged a new kernel after last deploy.

aj: which merge was that? I can start a bisect.

perf-bot: Last successful nightly before regression: 1742064000. Suspected merge: commit 9c7f3b4 (pr/2156) merged 1742099200 — contains batching heuristic tweak.

simon: @aj fwiw the batching change reduced max-batch wait to 8ms -> 4ms for low-latency paths. Could increase small-batch overhead.

maria: also saw higher KV cache evictions in pod logs around 03:05. eviction_rate jumped from 0.2% -> 4%. might cause cache-miss extra tokens and longer kernel paths.

aj: starting local bisect on canary image. reproducer: replay workload with many long-context chat sessions (seq len ~2048) — that's where p99 moved.

olivia: I pulled perf profile from the failing canary: hot path shows extra memcpy in attention kernel selection branch. attaching snippet:

```
# sampling profile
17.4%  attention_kernel_selector.cpp:select_kernel()
  -> memcpy +10ms for large sequences when switching to fp16-kernel
  -> increased if kv-cache miss
```

leo: that points to poor kernel switch penalty. maybe the selector doesn't check cache-friendly layout. Could be interaction between batching change and kernel slot allocation.

maria: hypothesis: batching change created more fragmented batches so selector switches kernels mid-request causing memcpy and cache churn.

aj: bisect results: commit 9c7f3b4 reproduces the spike, reverting locally to previous batching config returns p99 to baseline.

olivia: CI perf check also failed on the merge: https://ci.redwood/builds/2891 — perf_regression test p99 +33%. Looks correlated.

simon: tagging @eng-releases — this blocks rolling the release. recommend reverting the batching tweak in pr/2156 and open follow-up to adjust kernel-selector to be stable across batch composition.

maria: I can open the revert PR now, include the bisect logs, profile, and KV eviction stats.

aj: also adding a unit perf test that simulates fragmented batches and checks kernel-change cost.

leo: quick mitigation: increase batch wait back to 8ms on canary to reduce fragmentation; will patch autoscaler rollout.

simon: agreed. If revert PR approved, hold release and update rollout policy. @people-ops jk :) :thumbsup:

maria: PR opened: https://git.redwood/r/3314 revert pr/2156 — added notes and perf traces. Please review.

perf-bot: Update: alert A-6221 suppressed while revert in progress. Follow-up tasks: adjust kernel-selector heuristics, add perf unit for fragmented batches, monitor KV eviction trend. (reaction :eyes:)
